clue.text: Pants and takes the line of least resistance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short trousers, or in British usage underpants

definitions.text: takes the line of least resistance
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an electrical circuit that ... lets current take the easiest path

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses of one word: the garment, and the verb for a short circuit, where current finds the path of least resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts are a garment, and a circuit that shorts lets current bypass the intended load.

clue.text: Heroin: flop as a great leveller

parts.note: H is slang for heroin
a bomb is a theatrical flop, in British usage

explanation.surface: A heroin flop is said to reduce everyone to the same level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great leveller' is usually death, but here it is a weapon that flattens cities.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrogen bomb flattens everything for miles, literally levelling a city.

clue.text: Delivery system describing Prince Charles to an audience

indicators.note: to an audience means spoken aloud, so the description is heard, not spelt

parts.note: Prince Charles is a royal male

explanation.surface: A mail service that describes Prince Charles for listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Charles is a royal male; 'to an audience' means say that aloud. Royal Mail is Britain's postal service.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Mail is the British postal service, which delivers letters and parcels.

clue.text: What Brillo Pad did: cursed pitifully about sod all

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the other piece
pitifully means in a sorry state, so the letters of cursed are jumbled

parts.note: sod all is British slang for nothing, zero, O

explanation.surface: Brillo, nickname of broadcaster Andrew Neil, swore pathetically over nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brillo Pad' hints at Andrew Neil, nicknamed Brillo for his wiry hair; a Brillo pad is a soapy steel-wool pad. 'pitifully' turns CURSED into SCURED, and 'about' puts it around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brillo pad is a steel-wool kitchen pad used to scrub pans clean.

clue.text: Leading film villain like Dolly Parton?

parts.note: top means leading, as in the top team
a heavy is the actor cast as the villain or thug

explanation.surface: A cinema bad guy who outranks the rest is compared to the country singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly Parton, the American country singer, is famous for her large bust, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-heavy describes something with too much weight high up, a cheeky nod to the singer's figure.

clue.text: Outstandingly good article on boxer possibly over the head of Sun-reader, tosh

parts.note: the is the definite article
a boxer is a breed of dog

indicators.note: head of means take the first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Sun-reader
bollocks is British slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A tabloid piece on a boxer, above a Sun reader's head, is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of' takes S from Sun-reader; the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper. 'the dog's bollocks' is crude British slang for the very best.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog's bollocks is vulgar British slang for something excellent, the best of its kind.

clue.text: Hookers, given salesman's erection, do very well

parts.note: pros is slang for prostitutes

indicators.note: erection means something raised up, so in a down answer the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a salesman

explanation.surface: Prostitutes thrive after a salesman becomes aroused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erection' is the cheeky reversal signal: in a down answer REP raised up reads PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or succeed financially.

clue.text: Frame, with no difficulty, Latvia's premier

parts.note: ease means lack of difficulty

indicators.note: premier means first, so take the leading letter of Latvia

parts.note: the first letter of Latvia

explanation.surface: Latvia's prime minister is set up without any trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'premier' looks like a prime minister, but it means first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a wooden stand that holds a painting, a frame for the canvas.

clue.text: Hospital cut that will result in an unproductive future

definitions.text: Hospital cut that will result in an unproductive future

parts.words: Hospital cut that will result in an unproductive future
parts.note: reads like a hospital budget cut, but describes a surgical snip ending a man's fertility

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests NHS spending cuts; the 'cut' is a minor operation and 'unproductive' means no children.
explanation.definitionFit: A vasectomy is surgery cutting the sperm ducts, making a man sterile.

clue.text: Rib about dozy, ill-conceived Dome feature

indicators.note: the bone word goes about, that is around, the scrambled letters

parts.note: a rib is a bone

indicators.note: badly thought out, so the letters of dozy are put together wrongly

explanation.surface: A sneer at a sleepy, badly planned attraction at the Millennium Dome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rib' looks like teasing, but it is the bone itself; 'ill-conceived' scrambles the sleepy word to ODYZ and 'about' wraps the bone round it. The Body Zone was an exhibit in London's Millennium Dome in 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: The Body Zone was one of the themed exhibition areas inside the Millennium Dome.

clue.text: Pop group enough to tum one to drink?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., the Manchester band of the Gallagher brothers

definitions.text: enough to tum one to drink?
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a desert ... is where a traveller turns to drink water

explanation.walkthrough: The band is 'enough to drive one to drink'; the second sense is literal, a water source in the desert. 'tum' is the source's typo for 'turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oasis was a 1990s British rock band, and an oasis is a fertile watering place in a desert.

clue.text: Reported fit though he was relatively wiped out

indicators.note: said aloud, so the word for fit is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A man was healthy yet his relatives finished him off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported' means ABLE said aloud. 'relatively' is the joke: Abel was killed by a relative, his brother Cain.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Abel is murdered by his brother Cain, so he was wiped out by a relation.

clue.text: Supposed puctias of the peace sticking one in balls, flower — lousy things!

indicators.note: sticking one in means pushing it into the middle of the other word

parts.note: balls means nonsense, rot
I is the Roman numeral one
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is Italy's longest
lice are what make someone lousy

explanation.surface: An abusive rant about keepers of order, full of rude insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking one in balls' puts I into ROT. The source prints 'puctias', a garble of a word like custodians; riot police are 'supposed' keepers of the peace, the setter's dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Riot police are officers trained to control unruly crowds, supposedly keeping public order.

clue.text: It helps some people come out with ideas about cross

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Something helps shy people speak up, bringing ideas round to a cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come out' reads as speaking up or declaring oneself, but 'come' belongs to the definition and 'out' shuffles IDEAS with X. 'about' only says the X sits in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sex aid is a device that helps a person reach orgasm, which is the crude sense of come.

clue.text: A magnificent organ on dog — it's for cosmetic purposes

parts.note: Eye, the magazine Private Eye calling itself a magnificent organ (an organ is a publication); also an eye is a body organ
to dog someone is to follow them, to shadow

explanation.surface: A boast about a fine newspaper sitting on a dog, and some make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye, where this puzzle ran, is the 'magnificent organ'; 'on' puts it first in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is make-up brushed on the eyelids, purely for looks.

clue.text: Get lost, stupid Open University!

parts.note: screwy means crazy, foolish
OU is the abbreviation for the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: An angry dismissal hurled at a distance-learning university.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University teaches by post and broadcast in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw you is a rude way of telling someone to go away, much like get lost.

clue.text: Bush rambling about Kabul to Western Alliance initially

indicators.note: about means around in any order, so the letters are moved about
initially means take only the first letter of Alliance

parts.note: the first letter of Alliance

explanation.surface: President Bush wanders on about Kabul and the Western alliance in the Afghan war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like George W Bush, but it is the Australian outback. 'initially' takes only the A of Alliance, and 'about' is the anagram signal, not a container, making ALKABOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is an Aboriginal Australian's journey on foot through the outback, a long wander in the bush.

clue.text: As indulged in by Fitzgerald having it off and invading Cook's preserve?

definitions.text: As indulged in by Fitzgerald having it off and invading Cook's preserve?

indicators.note: invading means going inside the abbreviation for the Foreign Office

parts.note: FO, the Foreign Office, run by Robin Cook as Foreign Secretary from 1997
Ella Fitzgerald, the jazz singer

indicators.note: off here means turned away, so the little word it is read backwards

explanation.surface: A smutty line about the singer having sex and barging into a minister's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns IT into TI; ELLA and TI go 'invading' FO. Robin Cook, Foreign Secretary from 1997, was exposed for an affair, so the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellatio is oral sex performed on a man, the kind of activity the clue's having it off points to.

clue.text: It's capital here, rudely interrupting Brown

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of the other word

parts.note: tan is a light brown

indicators.note: rudely means roughly, so the letters of here are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone praising a place is rudely cut off by Gordon Brown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' suggests Gordon Brown, but it is the colour. 'rudely' gives EHER from HERE, and 'interrupting' puts it into TAN. Teheran is an older spelling of Tehran.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, now usually Tehran, is the capital city of Iran.

clue.text: They're produced by suspenders of French sexual conquests

parts.note: de is French for of
lays is slang for sexual partners

explanation.surface: Stockings and suspender belts help a Frenchman's seductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspenders' looks like the lingerie, but here means people who suspend things, and suspending causes delays.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to put it off, so those who suspend things cause postponements.

clue.text: Fergie, large figure, socially acceptable on the game

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
U means upper-class, socially acceptable, in the British U and non-U distinction
chess is the game

explanation.surface: Sarah Ferguson, with a hefty figure and good breeding, is a prostitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the game' is British slang for working as a prostitute, but here the game is simply chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Fergie is the nickname of Sarah Ferguson, who became the Duchess of York.

clue.text: As one adored by retailers, Posh sadly takes a break with Chip

indicators.note: sadly means unfortunately arranged, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: hol is a short form of holiday, a break
IC, short for integrated circuit, is a computer chip

explanation.surface: Victoria Beckham, known as Posh, takes a holiday with a fried chip.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh Spice, Victoria Beckham, is famous for shopping, but 'sadly' rearranges POSH and A into SHOPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopaholic is a compulsive shopper, the customer every store owner loves.

clue.text: Lofty operator responsible for Blair being without one-to one

indicators.note: without means outside, so the Prime Minister's letters go around the others

parts.note: Tony Blair was PM, the Prime Minister
an means one
a means one

explanation.surface: A grand figure is blamed for Blair missing a private meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one-to one' looks like a private meeting, but it gives two words for one with 'to' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan Am was an American airline, a company operating high in the sky.

clue.text: Dewar's effectively hiding his real mouthpiece?

indicators.note: hiding means the word lies inside the letters of these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Dewar's and the start of effectively

explanation.surface: Donald Dewar's speeches conceal the person who truly speaks for him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' signals letters concealed in Dewar's effectively. Donald Dewar was Scotland's First Minister; the question mark flags a rude joke about talking out of one's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk out of one's backside is to talk rubbish, so that part becomes the true mouth.

clue.text: Small organ but streak

parts.note: sm is an abbreviation for small
the ear is an organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A little body part, yet it runs naked across a pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'streak' hints at running naked, but here it is a streak of dirt or paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A smear is a mark drawn out across a surface, as is a streak of paint.

clue.text: Consumer's popular in bloody back

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other word
back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: red is the colour of blood, bloody
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A shopper is fashionable but has a bloody back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer's' reads as possessive but is 'consumer is'; 'back' reverses the colour of blood to DER and 'in' places the fashionable word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diner is someone eating a meal, a consumer of food.

clue.text: American people cause pop star who's getting on all right to take amphetamines

parts.note: Cher, the American singer, still performing well into her fifties
OK means all right
E is ecstasy, an amphetamine-type drug; two of them give EE

explanation.surface: Americans prompt an ageing singer to take speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' links the drugs onto the end of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American nation originally from the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: In which it's hard to choose the features of Split Personalities

definitions.text: In which it's hard to choose

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a split personality is pictured as ... in one person

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense needs 'in' from the idiom 'in two minds'; the second is a literal image of a divided personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of two minds is the idiom for indecision, and a divided personality would literally have a pair of minds.

clue.text: To be a father without, note, Tony's capital produces irony

indicators.note: without means outside, so the fathering word goes around the others

parts.note: to sire is to father a child
A is a musical note

indicators.note: a capital letter is the leading one, so take the first letter of Tony

parts.note: Tony Blair, the Prime Minister of the day

explanation.surface: Fatherhood without Tony Blair's money produces an ironic situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but means the capital letter T; 'without' puts SIRE outside A and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire uses irony and ridicule to mock, so the two are close cousins in comic writing.
